options.text: A range of values likely to contain a population parameter.
A single value used to estimate a population parameter.
The standard deviation of a sample.

questions.explanation: A point estimate is a single value that serves as an estimate of a population parameter, such as the sample mean for the population mean.

distractorRationale.a: This describes an interval estimate, not a point estimate.
distractorRationale.c: This describes a sample statistic, not an estimate.
distractorRationale.d: This is a misinterpretation of confidence intervals.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct formula for the standard error of the sample mean?
questions.explanation: The standard error of the sample mean is calculated using the sample standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.

distractorRationale.a: This formula incorrectly uses \( n \) instead of \( \sqrt{n} \).
distractorRationale.c: This formula incorrectly uses the population standard deviation \( \sigma \) instead of the sample standard deviation \( s \).
distractorRationale.d: This uses the population standard deviation \( \sigma \) instead of the sample standard deviation \( s \).

questions.stem: Calculate the standard error of the sample mean for a sample with a standard deviation of 4 and a size of 16. Provide your answer to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The standard error is calculated as \( \text{SE}(\bar{x}) = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{16}} = 1.00 \).

questions.stem: What does a 95% confidence interval mean?

options.text: There is a 95% probability that the population parameter is within the interval.
95% of the sample data falls within the interval.
If we take many samples, 95% of the confidence intervals will contain the true parameter.
The sample mean is within 95% of the interval range.

questions.explanation: A 95% confidence interval means that if we were to take many samples, about 95% of the intervals calculated would contain the true population parameter.

distractorRationale.a: Confidence intervals do not give the probability of containing the parameter for a specific sample.
distractorRationale.b: This misinterprets the interval as being about the data, not the parameter.
distractorRationale.d: This confuses the interval's purpose with the sample mean's placement.

questions.stem: A sample of 25 observations has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the population mean. Provide the lower bound of the interval.
questions.explanation: The standard error is \( \frac{5}{\sqrt{25}} = 1 \). The z-score for 95% confidence is 1.96. The interval is \( 50 \pm 1.96 \times 1 \), giving a lower bound of 48.04.

questions.stem: Which of the following affects the width of a confidence interval?
questions.explanation: The width of a confidence interval is influenced by the sample size, as it affects the standard error. Larger samples lead to narrower intervals.

distractorRationale.b: The sample mean affects the center, not the width of the interval.
distractorRationale.c: The population mean is unknown and does not affect the interval width.
distractorRationale.d: The sample median is not used in calculating confidence intervals.

questions.stem: Explain why increasing the sample size reduces the width of a confidence interval.
markingGuide: Larger sample size decreases standard error.
Smaller standard error reduces interval width.
More data provides a more precise estimate of the population parameter.
questions.explanation: Increasing the sample size reduces the standard error because the standard error is inversely proportional to the square root of the sample size. A smaller standard error results in a narrower confidence interval, reflecting a more precise estimate of the population parameter.

questions.stem: For a sample size of 36 with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 12, calculate the upper bound of a 90% confidence interval for the population mean. Provide your answer to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The standard error is \( \frac{12}{\sqrt{36}} = 2 \). The z-score for 90% confidence is 1.645. The interval is \( 100 \pm 1.645 \times 2 \), giving an upper bound of 102.80.

questions.stem: Describe the relationship between confidence level and confidence interval width.
markingGuide: Higher confidence level increases interval width.
More confidence requires a wider range to ensure parameter inclusion.
questions.explanation: A higher confidence level increases the width of the confidence interval because it requires a wider range to ensure that the interval captures the true population parameter with the specified level of confidence.
